fields.name: ClusterOfContent
fields.evidence: ls::HashMap (64 bytes): creator bg3.exe+0x3E72FD0 zeroes 0x40 bytes; destructor bg3.exe+0x5C4870 frees the value storage at +0x30 without element destructor and destroys the plain-key HashSet at +0 (bg3.exe+0x582AD0). Windows ClusterLoadHelper<ClusterVisualLoaderSystem::LoadOps> (bg3.exe+0x3E6CA60, gets the singleton through bg3.exe+0x3E6EC40 = query DAT_1463d3bec) inserts the 8-byte entity handles of each cluster's ClusterContentComponent key array (+0x20, 8-byte stride) with FUN_141d3c100 and stores an 8-byte value per key: '*(undefined8 *)(*(longlong *)(map + 0x30) + idx * 8) = ...'; key array read as 8-byte elements at +0x20/+0x2C. macOS ProcessContentChanges (bg3_macos_x64+0x6BBC590) compares the value (an ls::ID<EntityHandleTraits>) with the cluster entity being processed and removes keys of removed content; its destructor names the key table ls::HashTable<ls::ID<ecs::EntityHandleTraits>, ls::ClusterHashTableOps>. So: content entity -> the cluster entity that owns it. Note: the game hashes these keys with ClusterHashTableOps (key % bucket count) - the layout is that of Script Extender's HashMap, lookups from Lua must use the same hash.

summary: Client streaming singleton: a large hash map (tens of thousands of entries) used by the cluster visual loader (ls::ClusterVisualLoaderSystem); lives from game start.
open_questions: Name of the map member (not in any game data); 'ClusterOfContent' describes what the code does.
Script Extender's HashMap<EntityHandle,...> lookup must hash like ls::ClusterHashTableOps (plain value % bucket count) for Lua lookups to work - check before exposing find().
second_pass: Settled as HashMap<EntityHandle, EntityHandle>: the Windows cluster loader (bg3.exe+0x3E6CA60) inserts 8-byte content-entity keys and writes 8-byte values at +0x30, the Windows destructor shows trivial values, and the macOS ProcessContentChanges shows the value is the owning cluster entity.
